new_exact_v1_reviews.title: GhostServe: A Lightweight Checkpointing System in the Shadow for Fault-Tolerant LLM Serving
new_exact_v1_reviews.problem: The rise of million-token, agent-based applications has placed unprecedented demands on large language model (LLM) inference services.
new_exact_v1_reviews.old_path_and_changed_constraint: The stateful key-value (KV) cache, which grows with the sequence length, presents a central challenge as it is a critical and vulnerable component in distributed serving systems.
new_exact_v1_reviews.mechanism_and_ownership: In this work, we propose GhostServe, a novel checkpointing solution to facilitate fault-tolerant LLM serving.
new_exact_v1_reviews.evaluation_contract: Evaluations demonstrate that GhostServe reduces checkpointing latency by up to 2.7x and recovery latency by 2.1x for a single batch, and 1.2x median response latency compared to existing methods, in the presence of system failures, paving the way for high-availability and cost-effective LLM serving at scale.
new_exact_v1_reviews.proof_and_nonproof: Evidence is author-reported exact-v1 mechanism/evaluation evidence. It does not establish cross-model, cross-hardware, cross-workload or production generality unless those conditions are explicitly named above.
new_exact_v1_reviews.tradeoffs_and_failure_modes: The long-running nature of these tasks increases their susceptibility to hardware and software faults, leading to costly job failures, wasted resources, and degraded user experience.
new_exact_v1_reviews.coexistence_boundary: The older path remains appropriate where its workload and SLO do not trigger the changed constraint; the paper is treated as a conditional branch, not a universal replacement.

new_exact_v1_reviews.title: BRITE: A Benchmark for Reliable and Interpretable T2V Evaluation on Implausible Scenarios
new_exact_v1_reviews.problem: The rapid advancement of photorealistic Text-to-Video (T2V) generation brings in an urgent need for up-to-date evaluation methods.
new_exact_v1_reviews.old_path_and_changed_constraint: Existing benchmarks largely overlooked implausible scenarios and do not measure audio-visual alignment.
new_exact_v1_reviews.mechanism_and_ownership: We introduce BRITE, the first framework that unifies (1) implausible prompting, (2) fine-grained assessment of audio-visual consistency, and (3) QA-based interpretable evaluation into a comprehensive T2V benchmark.
new_exact_v1_reviews.evaluation_contract: The rapid advancement of photorealistic Text-to-Video (T2V) generation brings in an urgent need for up-to-date evaluation methods.
new_exact_v1_reviews.proof_and_nonproof: Evidence is author-reported exact-v1 mechanism/evaluation evidence. It does not establish cross-model, cross-hardware, cross-workload or production generality unless those conditions are explicitly named above.
new_exact_v1_reviews.tradeoffs_and_failure_modes: Our framework offers the community a reliable, interpretable benchmark and evaluation framework that can detect and locate limitations in the next generation of T2V models, especially for off-manifold prompts.
new_exact_v1_reviews.coexistence_boundary: The older path remains appropriate where its workload and SLO do not trigger the changed constraint; the paper is treated as a conditional branch, not a universal replacement.
